a: Politics — [Progress of Parliamentary Movement in Japan]
t: 1. The Emperor's oath, on the occasion of his accession, that "public matters shall be decided by public assembly."

a: Politics — [Progress of Parliamentary Movement in Japan]
t: 2. In 1873 Itagaki and others petitioned the Government to take steps for realizing the Imperial Oath.

a: Politics — [Progress of Parliamentary Movement in Japan]
t: 3. In 1880 a national organization for promoting the cause of popular rights was effected and in its name a petition was submitted to the Emperor for the immediate establishment of a parliament.

a: Politics — [Progress of Parliamentary Movement in Japan]
t: 4. In 1880 Provincial Assembly Regulations were enacted and popular craving was partially satisfied.

a: Politics — [Progress of Parliamentary Movement in Japan]
t: 5. In 1881 Itagaki and his fellow-politicians organized the Liberal Party, and passed a resolution to push the movement with vigor.

a: Politics — [Progress of Parliamentary Movement in Japan]
t: 6. In the same year a proclamation was issued announcing the establishment of a national assembly ten years hence.

a: Politics — [Progress of Parliamentary Movement in Japan]
t: 7. In 1882 Okuma organized the Progressive Party.

a: Politics — [Progress of Parliamentary Movement in Japan]
t: 8. In 1884 the Civic Corporation Regulations were enacted.

a: Politics — [Progress of Parliamentary Movement in Japan]
t: 9. On February 11th, 1889, the Constitution was promulgated.

a: Politics — [Progress of Parliamentary Movement in Japan]
t: 10. In October of the following year the first session of the Diet was convoked.
